tossups.text: The coefficients kappa-sub-e-minus, kappa-sub-oh-plus, and kappa-sub-tr are measured in experiments searching for violations of this property, which includes using optical-optical double resonance to measure the doppler shift of lithium ions. Any quantum field theory with this property and a Hermitian Hamiltonian must have CPT symmetry. This property is related to the conservation of the center of mass according to Noether's theorem. The fact that the Lagrangian of the electromagnetic field has this property means that Maxwell's equations can be written in a covariant form. The proper time has this property because it doesn't change with the reference frame. For 10 points, name this property of some quantities that don't change when boosting or rotating in Minkowski space.

This river receives the Green River in Canyonlands National Park before flowing downstream into Lake Powell. Low water levels in Lake Mead, which this river flows through, have raised concern of a "dead pool" when this river will not be able to flow through Hoover Dam. This river forms the border between California and Arizona. The Grand Canyon was carved by, for 10 points, what river named for a Rocky Mountain state?

In an opera by this composer, one character teases another for being sent to the military by singing the aria "Non più andrai" ("known pyoo ahn-DRY") to his page. In that opera by this composer, a "little song on the breeze" is sung as Susanna dictates a letter that will eventually expose the infidelity of Count Almaviva, whose valet is the opera's title character. In another of this composer's operas, the notoriously difficult aria "Der Hölle Rache" ("dair HUR-luh RAH-khuh") is sung by the Queen of the Night, whose attendants give Prince Tamino the opera's title instrument in the first act. For 10 points, name this Austrian composer of The Marriage of Figaro and The Magic Flute.

This civilization's thinkers developed a belief in material monism, the idea that all objects in the world are made of a single "first element." One such thinker from this civilization, Anaximenes [ah-nax-ih-men-ees], believed that that element was air; another thinker, Thales [thay-lees], believed it was water. For ten points, name this civilization whose natural philosophers from Miletus inspired its later schools, such as the Lyceum of Aristotle in Athens.

The Greek philosopher Democritus suggested these existed, and provided them a name that meant "uncuttable" in Greek. The plum-pudding model tried to explain these, but a later discovery of the positively-charged nucleus of these things disproved that model. There are three of these things in a molecule of water; two of hydrogen and one of oxygen. For 10 points, name this basic unit of every chemical element.

To determine whether a relation is one of these objects, you can check if each element in the domain has exactly one corresponding elementin the range, using the vertical line test. During one of these phenomena, low-level shear aligned by updrafts is penetrated by cold air from the downdraft, creating "hook echo" patterns on Doppler radar. In an initiation into a "cult" named for these objects, Koyemsis shriek at the blood produced when children are whipped. Barton Wright classifies the production of these objects into Early Traditional, Late Traditional, Early Action, and Late Action periods. Several of them are presented to brides in the midsummer Niman ceremony. One category of these objects gets increasingly more three-dimensional in four successive stages as they are awarded to infants, toddlers, slightly older toddlers, and finally boys and girls who are two years old; those objects are typically hung from rafters of homes. The wuya and the tithu are specialized kinds of these objects. Murals in kiva rooms depicted the likenesses of these objects, which are imitated by namesake masked dancers. They represent spirits or features from the natural world. For 10 points, name these spiritually significant dolls in Hopi religion.
acceptableAnswers: wuya and tithu before their mentions

tossups.text: In a novel by this author, the protagonist dedicates a meal of dark bread and meat with licorice sauce served on dark plates by nude black mistresses, in honor of his lost virility. tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for cortisol functions. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this adrenal-related structure.

tossups.text: After a crowd in this city threw snowballs at Thomas Preston's soldiers, Crispus Attucks was killed. The Intolerable Acts were passed in response to an event in this city in which members of the Sons of Liberty dressed as Mohawk Indians. British soldiers committed a 1770 massacre in this city, where rebels threw crates into the Atlantic Ocean in a namesake "Tea Party." For 10 points, name this capital of Massachusetts.

Systems that don't conform to this physicist's paradigms are classified as dilatant or pseudoplastic, and may be rheopectic or thixotropic. A law derived by this physicist assumes a constant viscosity. Flubber and oobleck are examples of fluids that don't conform to this physicist's model. For 10 points, name this scientist whose other contributions to physics include three laws of motion.

Economies of scale may create the high barriers to entry in this situation, in which the producer is not a price-taker. For 10 points, identify this condition contrasted with perfect competition in which a market is dominated by a single producer.

He notably used parabolic rather than pointed arches in designing a school for female Catholic teachers, while Domènec Sugranes completed his unfinished work on the Bellesguard. He created a crypt, Palau, and Parque for the Güell family, and he mixed the Gothic and Mudéjar styles in a building built for the factory owner Vicens. He may be better known for a building sometimes called "The Quarry" situated on a corner lot and featuring a sand-like wavy façade, as well as a still unfinished Roman Catholic church, both of which are in Barcelona. According to Marden's theorem, a function with roots at the vertices of one of these objects has zero derivative at the foci ["FOH-sy"] of that object's Steiner inellipse ["in-ellipse"]. The area of one of these shapes can be calculated by Heron's formula. Euclidean distance obeys an "inequality" named for these shapes, which are called "scalene" if they have all different side lengths. For 10 points, name these polygons with three edges and three vertices.
